text: USER REVOCATION (round-24, supersedes the round-11 sort requirement from the liveliness task): the sort-working-agents-to-top feature is REMOVED — in live use it reshuffles constantly and flickers (status flaps defeat the stability window; screenshots on record). NO dynamic re-sorting of tabs inside the orchestrator group, NO FLIP/reorder animation. Replacement is this task's taxonomy: STATIC order — Managers section (planner first, future watchers) then Workers in stable spawn order. Liveliness stays only as row TREATMENTS (brightness/wash/task-line/dots), never position. Additional scope for this task: DELETE sortHierarchyNodes, the stability-window code, and the FLIP animation wiring entirely (no dead code left); apply a ~2s display-debounce to the working-row TREATMENTS so the same status flap that broke sorting does not make the wash/dots blink.

CODE-WALK EVIDENCE for the re-sort removal (exact map, verified in landed source). DEFECT A — stability window structurally defeated: HierarchyTree.tsx keeps sort state in a component ref (sortStateRef, line ~239); any REMOUNT of the tree resets it to null, and sortHierarchyNodes.ts line 69-73 then takes the prevPending===undefined branch which commits the LIVE status IMMEDIATELY for every pane — so each remount (sidebar snapshot updates recreate the subtree) produces an instant re-sort, bypassing the 2s window entirely. DEFECT B — the 'FLIP' animation fires on ANY layout shift, not just reorders: the useLayoutEffect (HierarchyTree.tsx ~250-266) compares getBoundingClientRect().top per row against a prevTops map and animates translateY on ANY delta — rows slide 320ms whenever anything ABOVE them changes height (plan entry appearing, tabs added, sections expanding), even with zero reordering. This is the constant 'переставляется туда-сюда' the user filmed. DEFECT C — upstream status flap: the statuses record flips Working<->Idle on chat-turn cadence (output silence -> Idle within seconds, next token -> Working), so rank churn is by design of the tracker — which is why POSITION must never derive from status. DELETION LIST (complete): src/components/Sidebar/sortHierarchyNodes.ts + sortHierarchyNodes.test.ts (whole files); HierarchyTree.tsx: the sortHierarchyNodes/HierarchySortState imports (~12-14), sortStateRef + prevTops + rowRefs animation machinery, the useMemo sort block (~241-246), the useLayoutEffect top-delta block (~250-266). KEEP: statusSortRank nothing — Managers/Workers static grouping replaces it; treatments debounce reuses the pending/committed PATTERN (2s) applied to visual state only, or plain CSS transitions on the treatment properties (worker's call, cheapest honest option wins).

SCOPE ADDITION (round-30, user): the composer context strip trio completes — Planner panes show 'Planning: <plan title>' above the input, exactly the same component family and behavior as the existing 'Orchestrating: <plan>' strip (same placement, same click-through to the plan, same styling grammar; workers already show 'Working on: <task>'). Derive from planner_ref binding (the pane bound as a plan's planner shows the strip for THAT plan). One shared strip component with a role-driven label — do not fork a planner variant. Criterion: spawn a pair on dev -> the planner pane shows 'Planning: <plan>' above its input, click opens the plan (screenshot in report).

Planner panes need composer strip 'Planning: <plan title>' above the input, same shared component/behavior as Orchestrating strip; derive from planner_ref, role-driven label, no fork. Relayed to Dali/Hopper on eight.

Accepted taxonomy lane origin/lane/sidebar-taxonomy f1a0fb48 and merged locally as ab546019. Local gates: focused Sidebar/Composer TS tests, tsc, file-size, diff-check. Dali gates included cargo check/fmt, prompts 13/0, orchestration_pair 9/0, Playwright screenshot.

BOUNCE FINDINGS (round-32, user screenshot of the landed state): (1) ROLE BADGE DOES NOT FIT — 'ORCHESTRAT…' truncates in the bubble; size the badge to the full word (smaller type/tracking or wider chip; 'Orchestrator' must render whole — truncated role labels defeat the entire purpose). (2) PLANNER HAS NO BADGE and (3) IS FILED UNDER WORKERS: the pane whose chat literally introduces itself as the Planner (under Orchestrator Byron) renders in the WORKERS section with no badge. ROOT CAUSE is backend: the planner is structurally AgentRole::Worker with the planner role_profile, so any mapping keyed on AgentRole alone classifies it as Worker. FIX: the role->section module must key on (role, role_profile, planner_ref match) — planner_ref binding OR role_profile=planner => Manager section + PLANNER badge; expose whatever field the frontend is missing in the pane snapshot (backend half of this lane). (4) CONTAINMENT UNREADABLE: managers/workers do not visually belong to their orchestrator — the sections must render NESTED under the owning orchestrator's tab (indent + the group's left containment line), not as flat global sections; with two orchestrators on screen (Main + Byron) flat sections are ambiguous by construction. Acceptance addition: a pair + one worker under Byron renders as Byron > Managers > [Kelvin PLANNER] / Workers > [worker], visually contained, while Main's group renders separately; badges never truncate at any of our three UI font scales.

ADDITION to the open bounce round (round-32b, user): the planner intro is a wall of agent-jargon ('draft GOAL, Spec, Plan structure, task briefs...') — inhuman for the user. SPLIT the two audiences: the agent CONTRACT stays as the collapsed machine-facing spawn brief (unchanged semantics); the USER-VISIBLE first message becomes a compact intro CARD, not a paragraph. PINNED COPY (implement verbatim, constants module):

PLANNER_INTRO_CARD — title: 'Planner — {plan_title}'; subtitle: 'working under {orchestrator_name}'; bullets:
- I turn your goal into a plan: requirements, phases, tasks with clear done-criteria
- I ask the right questions before work starts, so nobody builds on guesses
- Changed direction? Tell me — I reshape the plan, nothing is set in stone
footer: 'Planning input goes here; execution questions go to {orchestrator_name}.'

ORCH_GREETING stays as shipped ('Paired up — {planner} is my Planner. Tell me the goal…') — it is already human.

PRESENTATION: intro renders as a structured card in chat (icon + title + subtitle + tight bullet list + muted footer), same visual family as the existing Reminder card — NOT a text paragraph. The card is the pattern for any future role intro (watchers inherit it). Acceptance addition: pair spawn on dev -> planner chat shows the card (screenshot), the collapsed brief below it holds the full contract; no role-intro paragraph blobs remain.

ADDITIONS to the open bounce round (round-32c, user, three quick rulings): (1) WORKER rows show the provider glyph (логотипчик — which network/model family the worker runs on): provider icon before the name, same size grammar as agent tabs elsewhere. (2) MODEL RETURNS TO THE BUBBLE — revising the earlier model-to-tooltip ruling: the pair badges show role AND model together (e.g. chip pair 'ORCHESTRATOR' + 'OPUS', or one chip 'ORCHESTRATOR · OPUS' — whichever fits without truncation at all three font scales; the fit-whole rule from finding 1 applies to the combined form). Workers keep provider glyph + model chip as before. (3) Everything still fits: role+model must not reintroduce truncation — measure at the smallest scale.
